analysis:
The supplied PR changes only CHANGELOG.md. The patch (hunk @@ -193,11 +193,16 @@) adds four bullets under the 'Unreleased — cache reliability' section:
- Preserve negotiated healthy preload incumbents when response bodies are interrupted or readiness probes fail in transport.
- Align preload model-ID validation with the registration request bound.
- Keep configured catalogs above 128 models usable.
- Select a bounded, demand-driven tokenizer preload set when the verified catalog exceeds loaded-contract capacity, using incremental preload negotiation.

No source files, authorization paths, attestation logic, encryption, billing or admin code are included in this batch, so there is no executable security change visible here. I could not verify the described behavior against any code. The text asserts fail-closed behavior on protocol loss, no widening of cache-routing allowlists, and no waiting on preloading during inference. Those claims describe cache-reliability behavior in the Go coordinator and the Rust/sidecar tokenizer. That code is a likely place for the real security-relevant change, and it needs review wherever it appears in other batches or PRs.

Points for later review of the underlying code:
- Bound the demand-driven selection, which consumer demand could influence. Check for tenant isolation and fair replacement, and for resource-exhaustion limits (ADV-002).
- Confirm that preload/cache participation cannot cross account boundaries or affect T-041 cache oracle assumptions.
- Confirm that a model-ID length bound change does not enable oversized registration inputs (TB-002).

The changelog shows no concrete regression. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only diff.
